newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan utility to delay nuclear power plant--paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan utility to delay nuclear power plant--paper.

text.p: Tohoku Electric Power Co Inc expects public opposition to delay construction of a nuclear power plant in northern Japan and has taken the plant off its supply programme, a newspaper said on Thursday.
A company spokesman said he could not comment on plans for the Maki plant, ahead of an official announcement of the utility's 10-year electricity supply programme on March 31.
Tohoku Electric had originally planned to start building the Maki plant from fiscal 1999/2000 starting April 1, and to begin power generation in 2005/2006.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said Tohoku Electric had given up on its plans to start operating the plant in 2006/07 after a majority of Maki inhabitants returned a "no" vote in last year's referendum on the utility's plans for the plant.
Every year, electricity utilities draw up a 10-year electricity supply programme, which they submit to the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) at the end of March.
The paper said Tohoku Electric had omitted the Maki power plant from its 10-year programme starting 1997/98, expecting a delay of at least three years to its original plans.
The result of the referendum was not legally binding, but after the vote, the mayor of Maki decided not to sell the needed land to the power utility, effectively halting Tohoku Electric's plan.

Since then, a string of events -- an accident at a prototype fast-breeder-reactor in December 1995 involving leakage of sodium coolant followed by an explosion at a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant earlier this month, which exposed 35 workers to radiation -- has undermined public confidence in nuclear power.
Kyushu Electric Power Co In earlier this month said it had abandoned a plan to build a nuclear power plant in the southern city of Kushima due to local opposition.
